## Reproducing WLasso on breast cancer gene expression data (GSE2990)

### Data and preprocessing
We use data from the [Gene Expression Omnibus](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/) with GEO Accession GSE2990 as used by the authors (Zhu et al., 2020) of the paper [A variable selection approach for highly correlated predictors in high-dimensional genomic data](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btab114). The data contains $n = 189$ tumours and 22,283 probes (HG-U133A array: chip to measure human gene expression). The values range from 2.66 to 15.13, which is consistent with RMA-normalised data, meaning that the data is already processed.

```{r}
# Load the gene data from Gene Expression Omnibus
expr <- read.delim("GSE2990_series_matrix.txt",
                   comment.char = "!", row.names = 1)
dim(expr)

# Values appear to be normalized (between 2 and 15).
range(as.matrix(expr), na.rm = TRUE)
```


As in Zhu et al. (2021), we kept probes with IQR $\geq 1.5$ (1,155 probes) and removed probes without a gene annotation (49 removed, 1,106 left). 
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# First cleaning step: remove probes with IQR < 1.5
iqr_values <- apply(expr, 1, IQR)
# summary(iqr_values)
keep <- iqr_values >= 1.5
# sum(keep)
expr_filt <- expr[keep, ]
# dim(expr_filt)

# Second step: Remove genes without gene annotation
# BiocManager::install("hgu133a.db")
library(hgu133a.db)

probe_ids <- rownames(expr_filt)
symbols <- mapIds(hgu133a.db,
                  keys = probe_ids,
                  column = "SYMBOL",
                  keytype = "PROBEID",
                  multiVals = "first")

# sum(is.na(symbols))

# Remove
has_symbol <- !is.na(symbols)
expr_ann <- expr_filt[has_symbol, ]
symbols_ann <- symbols[has_symbol]

dim(expr_ann)
```


The ESR1 probe is a gene associated with breast cancer. We use it as the response $y$ and the remaining 1,105 probes as predictors $X$. As is convention in implementing Lasso regularizaiton, we standardized each predictor. We also mean-centred $y$. The paper reports $p = 1{,}111$, so our probe set differs slightly, $p = 1{,}106$.

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Use ESR1 gene as the gene to predict.
all_symbols <- mapIds(hgu133a.db,
                      keys = rownames(expr),
                      column = "SYMBOL",
                      keytype = "PROBEID",
                      multiVals = "first")

esr1_probes <- names(all_symbols)[all_symbols %in% "ESR1"]
# esr1_probes
# esr1_probes %in% rownames(expr_ann)

# Pull the ESR Variable left after IQR + Annotation filter and use as y
esr1_probe <- esr1_probes[1]
# esr1_probe
y <- as.numeric(expr_ann[esr1_probe, ])
expr_X <- expr_ann[rownames(expr_ann) != esr1_probe, ]

# length(y)
# dim(expr_X)

# Standardize X.
X <- scale(t(expr_X))
# dim(X)
# round(colMeans(X)[1:3], 6)
# apply(X, 2, sd)[1:3]

# Mean-center Y.
y_c <- y - mean(y)
# mean(y_c) # should be close to zero.
```


### Method
The model is $y = X\beta + \epsilon$ with $\mathrm{Cor}(X) = \Sigma$. WLasso whitens the predictors with $\tilde{X} = X\Sigma^{-1/2}$, so that $y = \tilde{X}\tilde\beta + \epsilon$ with $\tilde\beta = \Sigma^{1/2}\beta$, and the error term is unchanged. It then minimises the generalised Lasso criterion
$$\|y - \tilde{X}\tilde\beta\|_2^2 + \lambda \|\Sigma^{-1/2}\tilde\beta\|_1,$$
and thresholds the estimates to the top $K$ (for $\tilde\beta$) and top $M$ (for $\beta$) coefficients, with $K$ and $M$ chosen by an **MSE-ratio rule** controlled by $\gamma$. $\Sigma$ was estimated with the two-block structure of Section 2.5: $(\hat\alpha_1,\hat\alpha_2,\hat\alpha_3) = (0.19, 0.27, 0.55)$, against $(0.17, 0.21, 0.52)$ in the paper.

The paremeters the model takes are $\gamma$, which we set to 0.95 (between 0.9 and 0.99 recommended by the paper), and max_steps = 500 (the paper does not find significance difference in performance between 500 and 2000).

### A problem with the package and our patch
With the `WLasso` package (v1.0), `Whitening_Lasso()` returned an empty model on these data (the lowest MSE was at the first, all-zero step), although a plain Lasso on the same data selected 60 probes. The package works on its own example data. I used Claude Code to help me identify the issue: using the source, in the step that chooses $M$, the MSE is computed from the coefficients sorted by absolute value, not from the coefficients in their original order, so each coefficient multiplies the wrong column of $X$. We think this is a bug that does little harm when all correlations are positive, as in the paper's simulations. We changed that one argument in a copy of the function (not an official fix), and results below come from that modified copy.

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Install WLasso package
# install.packages("WLasso")
library(WLasso)
# help(package = "WLasso")
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Sigma Estimation
Sigma_est <- Sigma_Estimation(X)
round(Sigma_est$alpha, 2) # paper reports 0.17, 0.21 and 0.52, we get slightly different
# We get: 0.19 0.27 0.55

# Number of probes the clustering put into one of the two blocks
# We get 181 out of 1105
length(Sigma_est$group_act)

# Step 2: Model transformation
Sigma_estmat <- Sigma_est$mat
```

```{r}
# Fix bug on the paper
src <- paste(deparse(WLasso::Whitening_Lasso), collapse = "\n")
src2 <- gsub("x\\s*=\\s*beta_sort,\\s*sorted_vect\\s*=\\s*beta_sort",
             "x = beta_final0, sorted_vect = beta_sort", src)

# identical(src, src2)   # we want FALSE this time

WL_fixed <- eval(parse(text = src2))
environment(WL_fixed) <- asNamespace("WLasso")
# grep("beta_sort", strsplit(src, "\n")[[1]], value = TRUE)
# grep("beta_interm", strsplit(src2, "\n")[[1]], value = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Fit the model
# mod_fix <- WL_fixed(X = X, Y = y_c, Sigma = Sigma_estmat,
                    # gamma = 0.95, maxsteps = 500)

# range(mod_fix$mse)
# sum(mod_fix$beta.min != 0)
```

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# We also fit regular Lasso for comparison:
#install.packages("glmnet")
# library(glmnet)
# cvfit <- cv.glmnet(X, y_c)
# sum(coef(cvfit, s = "lambda.min")[-1] != 0)
# returns 60 coefficients!!!!
```

### Results
| Method | Probes | Genes |
|---|---|---|
| WLasso ($\gamma = 0.95$, patched) | 59 | 56 |
| Lasso (cross-validation) | 60 | 59 |

### Key takeaways

+ WLasso Works primarily for quantitative data, there is an MSE minimization that happens when fitting the Lasso.

+ The WLasso package presented some errors, so it might be better to fit the math directly rather than relying on the package.

+ ["WLogit" Package](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/WLogit/WLogit.pdf) developed by the same authors.


**Reference.** Zhu, W., Lévy-Leduc, C. and Ternès, N. (2021). A variable selection approach for highly correlated predictors in high-dimensional genomic data. *Bioinformatics*, 37(16), 2238–2244.
